source.title: Right Time to Learn:Promoting Generalization via Bio-inspired Spacing Effect in Knowledge Distillation
source.authors: Guang-Long Sun; Hong-Wei Yan; Li-Yuan Wang; Qian Li; Bo Lei; Yi Zhong

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests a spaced knowledge-distillation method, not the claim versions about random-label memorization, width, architecture, optimizer comparisons, large batches, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy gains and perturbation robustness for Spaced KD. These results concern a different training intervention and do not measure a listed claim version. Image-corruption and adversarial-attack results are out-of-distribution or attack robustness, outside the claim.
record.test_reason: Appendix A.7, Figure 5(b), reports classification accuracy across batch sizes 32–512 for online and Spaced KD, bearing on V5 in a distillation setting. The ResNet recipe specifies 80 epochs. However, the supplied text does not preserve the plotted curves, so the direction of the batch-size effect cannot be determined. The remaining experiments do not test a listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that Spaced KD improves online and self distillation across tested settings, and attribute the gains to flatter minima using theoretical analysis and parameter-perturbation experiments. They also identify later-stage timing as beneficial and leave adaptive interval selection unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces spaced knowledge distillation, a teacher-student training schedule; it does not use the original claim's random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports effects varying with space interval, when spaced distillation begins, loss function, KD method, dataset, architecture, learning rate, and batch size. It says later-stage initiation is more beneficial and that the naive constant-ahead teacher baseline shows no significant improvement over online KD.

fits_no_version.finding: Spaced KD generally improves held-out accuracy over corresponding KD baselines, although Table 3 reports an L1-loss exception: 69.54% without spacing versus 69.30% with spacing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spacing teacher updates can improve knowledge-distillation performance, with effects depending on the loss and training schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.4 reports smaller training-loss increases and higher training accuracy under Gaussian parameter perturbations for Spaced KD. The perturbations are not described as scaled to weight magnitudes, and generalization-gap rankings are not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spaced KD can improve robustness to unscaled parameter perturbations relative to online KD.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-corruption and BIM evaluations generally favor Spaced KD, with some corruption conditions showing decreases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spaced KD can improve corruption and adversarial robustness in the tested image classifiers.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025.
record.problems: The paper reports that results are averaged over three repeats, but the supplied text gives no uncertainty estimates for the principal accuracy tables. The Gaussian-perturbation evidence is described in text and plotted, without numerical values in the supplied text. The study evaluates KD performance rather than the listed claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: reported results concern the distinct Spaced KD intervention and do not measure a version in the claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Student-network width beyond the interpolation threshold. Varying teacher width while evaluating a fixed ResNet-18 student does not test this.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning-budget effects.
Language models, longer-training remedies, and controlled learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization remedies.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.

Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with measured generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Gaussian parameter noise and Hessian trace do not establish these.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals and retraining.

missing.what: Accuracy by batch size and spacing condition in Figure 5(b), including the online-KD baseline. The blanket exclusion in rows_left_out overlooks this batch-size comparison. Curve values and their direction are unavailable in the supplied text, preventing a supported verdict about a large-batch penalty or its removal.
missing.locator: Section 5.3, Learning Rate and Batch Size; Appendix A.7, Figure 5(b); Section 5.1 for the 80-epoch ResNet recipe

record.verdict_notes: No V5 verdict is assigned because Figure 5(b)'s curves cannot be read from the supplied text. The statement that spacing helps at batch sizes greater than 64 compares distillation methods; by itself it does not show whether increasing batch size harms accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under differing tuning budgets.
Large-batch generalization gaps under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
